chunks: Humeed ibn Ziyad, from Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah, from someone else, from Aban, from Abu Maryam, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
When a man gives charity, whether the recipient takes possession of it or does not take possession of it, knows about it or does not know, it is valid.
ai.seo_question: Is charity valid if the recipient doesn't know they received it?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to clarify that the validity of sadaqah hinges on the donor's intention and the act of giving, rather than the recipient's physical possession or awareness. This ruling underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on the internal sincerity (ikhlas) of the giver, ensuring that charity remains valid even if the recipient is unaware or the gift is not yet collected, thereby removing barriers to continuous charitable giving.
